Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, by source: a plugin can call the public runtime with deferTerminalLifecycle and extra callback properties, which the adapter spreads into the core runner and the new attempt code invokes after active-run registration. Is this the best way to solve the issue? No: the shared logical lifecycle owner is the right repair shape, but forwarding its host-only callbacks through the public plugin adapter violates the intended ownership boundary. nodes.body:
Thanks @zhangguiping-xydt!

**Proof:** On exact head `159efa92d2a26a38fa51ddeaf6afb4162d433450`, an isolated production Gateway received an injected HTTP 503 overload from the primary model. Embedded fallback delivered once with one successful terminal record. A real command-line child also delivered once without a stale embedded terminal record. While that child was running, `openclaw tasks cancel` returned success and the canonical task state changed from `running` to `cancelled` with an end time.

- **Bug:** A failed primary attempt could clear the active run before fallback work finished, so the task stayed running and cancellation could not reach it.
- **Fix:** One logical-turn owner now transfers cancellation and terminal state across embedded and command-line fallbacks, while the plugin facade rejects forged host lifecycle callbacks.

CI note: `checks-node-compact-large-8` hit one unrelated FIFO-read timeout. Its 28 tests passed on this head, the merge base, current main, and the failed-job rerun.

**Example**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Primary overload starts fallback; the task stays `running`; cancel times out. | Fallback remains reachable; completion records one terminal result; cancel changes the task to `cancelled`. |
